pool.text: La Nouvelle-Orleans was founded by the French Mississippi Company under Jean-Baptiste Le Moyne de Bienville.
The Code Noir was established to formalize harsh laws governing the lives of enslaved Africans.
The Ursuline sisters institution was founded by nuns sponsored by the Company of the Indies.
The Natchez revolt erupted with an attack on Fort Rosalie, resulting in numerous deaths.
France transferred possession of Louisiana to Spain in the Treaty of Paris.
Local residents staged the Louisiana Rebellion, briefly seizing control of the city from Spain.
A streetcar strike took place in the city, accompanied by serious public unrest.
The moniker The City that Care Forgot came into use to describe residents' carefree nature.
The historic streetcar line operating to Desire Street was converted into a bus line.
New Orleans adopted a home rule charter to establish its current mayor-council government.
One Shell Square was established as the tallest building in the city.
The Alliance Française of New Orleans was established as a cultural center for French speakers.
New Orleans was officially named the murder capital of America after hitting a peak.
The reality television program The Real World: New Orleans was set in the city.
Louisiana began offering tax incentives aimed at boosting film and television production.
The local hospitality industry employed 85,000 people and became the top economic sector.
Hurricane Katrina struck the city, causing catastrophic levee failures and massive flooding.
Hurricane Katrina struck the region and severely devastated the local transit service.
Louisiana voters adopted a constitutional amendment dedicating offshore drilling revenues to coastal restoration.
Tulane University converted McAlister Place on its Uptown campus into a pedestrian and bicycle mall.
